content.text:
I found no claims to flag: every claim in the document is backed by the record.

- **Root cause and causal chain:** the change removed the month-total update from `record_purchase` (D1). At the revision that ran, the other write path doesn't move that total either (S1). Six other places in the code still use the stored field (U1–U6). All three replicas were running that revision (T10).
- **Ruled-out deploy (P1):** the alert's oldest affected purchase, 04:09:00, comes 42 seconds after P2's deploy at 04:08:18. That supports clearing P1.
- **"Could see the same drift even after a rollback":** this holds, and it's hedged. D1's only change is inside `record_purchase`, so the month-deriving path was already in the earlier revision.
- **Contributing factor 3:** it is framed as Code-Fix's reading, and Code-Fix did say it. The record says the test file Code-Fix read on main is the same as at the deployed revision.
- **"No test run" / "no review" / "watched only by" the integrity check:** the record contains none of these things, so the absence claims stand.

One borderline call: the symptom line "Shoppers saw no failure" is stated flatly, even though error rate wasn't measured. I accepted it because the record says customer loss was "none so far" and the alert came from the integrity check, not from users.

I didn't judge the action items or the what-if halves of the "had it been otherwise" lines, as instructed.

supported.quote: The change took the total_this_month_cents update out of record_purchase, and the other write path, record_purchase_deriving_the_month, does not move it either, so every current-month purchase written afterwards left the stored month total short by its price.

The field still sits on the account and is still used: render_monthly_statement and _compared_with_usual read it, the_mean_purchase_this_month and average_spend_per_item_this_month divide it by a count of purchases, and reconcile_monthly_totals compares it with the sum of the current-month purchases.

A code change stopped the shop from updating each shopper's saved spending-this-month figure when they bought something, while the parts of the shop that show and check that figure still use the saved copy.

The month totals already saved short stayed wrong, and each new purchase this month could leave them further short, so monthly statements and spend summaries could keep showing shoppers figures that disagree with what they bought
a shopper routed through the month-deriving write path could see the same drift even after a rollback
Shoppers saw no failure, but their stored monthly spend totals stopped matching their purchases
No one using the shop was seen to hit a failure. What was seen instead: the spend-integrity check found that shoppers' stored month totals did not match the purchases behind them.

Purchases written after the onset were stored without moving the account's month total. At the revision that ran, record_purchase and record_purchase_deriving_the_month both append the purchase and add only to total_cents, so total_this_month_cents stayed where it was whichever path the purchase took.
That write path arrived with deploy P2 at {P2.1}, which removed the month-total update from record_purchase. All {T10.2} replicas were running that revision as of {T10.1}.
The earlier deploy P1: the alert dates the oldest affected purchase at {A4}, after P2 at {P2.1}, so the service did no harm while P1's revision was running.

The change stopped writing total_this_month_cents, but the field was kept and the code around it still uses the stored value: the monthly statement reads it in render_monthly_statement and _compared_with_usual, the_mean_purchase_this_month and average_spend_per_item_this_month divide it by a count of purchases, and reconcile_monthly_totals compares it with the sum of the current-month purchases.
Month-total drift was watched only by the spend-integrity check, which runs every {A5} days. The module itself says nothing in the write path notices when a total and the purchases disagree.
The SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile alert paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it.

supported.quote: An on-call person would have been asked straight away to take the rollback Argus left for a person, rather than it waiting.

By Code-Fix's reading, the test file at the deployed revision holds a test that pins record_purchase adding to the month total, which the deployed code no longer does. No test run before the deploy was seen.

No review was seen that checked who still uses total_this_month_cents before the change stopped writing it, even though the module's own docstring warns that a write moving one copy and not the other leaves two answers.
